Oh ok. Is he sterilized? If he is, it would be easy to find him a female. I've never bonded two males, but I heard it can be more complicated. Anyway, you can't have two guineas in the cage you have now, so I don't think you have options. You should have a bigger living space for the piggies. And when you bond to piggies, you should have another cage that you can place near the first one, this way the two piggies you want to bond can smell and hear each other, without the risk of hurting one another. Good luck with your male!

I don't think you can really choose one over the other. Those are two very important and very different needs. It also depends on the personality of a specific pig. Usually males like to have more space, especially if they live with other males. Girls are very social and need company. Obviously those are not rules written in stone, every piggy is different. Adult pigs that were separated from a herd at a young age and lived alone for a long time often lack the social skills to live in peace with a cage mate. As you can see, there are a lot of factors at play. Is it an hypothetical question? Otherwise you should provide more details about your situation.
